title: Egialeus
summary: Began a kingdom at Sicyon, in Greece, in the age Shuckford is describing. The year is one he reports as generally thought, with a footnote to Eusebius.
description: Added from the Shuckford import. Display only. Shuckford’s years are Anno Mundi, or a “years before Christ” figure he is reporting. This chronology never sets a sort, and no tier 1–4 chronology dates this person’s birth, so there is no sort year.

sorting_basis.note: No tier gives a birth year (Shuckford is display-only).

reign.date: about the fifteenth year of Belus, i. e. one hundred and sixty-five years after the first year of Nimrod’s kingdom, and one hundred and fifty years after Mizraim’s settlement in Egypt, A. M. 1922, Egialeus began a kingdom at Sicyon, in Greece
reign.citation: Shuckford, The Sacred and Profane History of the World Connected, 5th ed., revised by James Creighton (London: William Baynes, 1819), vol. 1, Book IV, p. 195 (facsimile PDF p. 291)
reign.note: He writes “it is generally thought”. Footnote to Eusebius, Chron. p. 19.
